Perusahaan Perseroan Persero PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara Posts Higher Revenues in Latest Quarter

Indonesia’s state-owned electric utility, Perusahaan Perseroan Persero PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN), reported higher revenues and stable operating profits in its latest quarterly results, buoyed by increased electricity demand from both residential and industrial sectors. The company, which supplies the majority of Indonesia’s electricity, said that total revenues reached IDR 98.3 trillion for the first quarter of 2024, a 7.2% increase compared to the same period last year.

PLN attributed the rise to robust demand across Java, Sumatra, and Kalimantan, as well as continued growth in new industrial connections. "Our ongoing efforts to expand infrastructure and improve reliability have supported higher consumption, especially in manufacturing and digital services sectors," said PLN President Director Darmawan Prasodjo during a virtual results briefing. He added, "We are seeing the positive impact of our investment in the transmission grid and a steady increase in customer numbers."

Operating profit for the quarter reached IDR 11.7 trillion, broadly in line with last year’s figure, as higher fuel costs were offset by efficiency programs and a favorable generation mix. The company noted that hydropower and geothermal units performed strongly due to favorable weather conditions, contributing to a more balanced energy portfolio and helping to keep generation costs in check.

Net profit for the quarter stood at IDR 5.1 trillion, up 3.4% year-on-year. Capital expenditure in the period totaled IDR 12.6 trillion, with significant investments directed toward renewable energy projects and grid modernization initiatives. "PLN’s financials remain solid, and the focus on renewables is in line with the government’s energy transition targets," said Vina Kartika, an analyst at Nusantara Capital Advisory.

The company’s total customer base rose to 85.7 million accounts, reflecting ongoing rural electrification efforts and a strong push for digital metering. Industry observers note that PLN’s results provide reassurance about the stability of Indonesia’s power sector amid broader economic uncertainty. "PLN’s performance highlights the resilience of utility demand and the importance of infrastructure investment," commented Dede Amir, spokesperson for the Indonesian Power Industry Association.

Looking ahead, PLN reaffirmed its full-year guidance and reiterated its commitment to supporting Indonesia’s economic development through reliable and sustainable electricity supply.
